versions.changelog:
This update brings together 2.0.2.0 to 2.0.9.0 from the beta channel.

If you use Live TV with the Native Tuner only, open the Live TV tab after updating and turn off the new "Publish Playlists" switch. It stays on for anyone who already had Live TV enabled, so an M3U tuner or TiviMate setup keeps working, but the native tuner does not need it.

Fixed: Request Delay now limits how fast the plugin talks to your provider in total. Each parallel worker used to apply it separately, so with Sync Parallelism at 10 and the default of 50 ms up to 200 requests a second could go out, enough for some providers to block your IP. It is now one shared gap per provider: 50 ms means at most 20 a second. When the provider says it is getting too many requests, every request to it waits. A first sync of a large library takes longer as a result; if your provider allows more, lower Request Delay. Setting it to 0 is no longer saved as 50 (reported by dillardblom).

Fixed: a single unreadable value from your provider, such as an empty value where a number belongs, no longer makes content disappear. It could blank a series' title, plot and TMDB id, drop every episode of a series, or make a whole category fail to sync. Such values are now ignored or read as 0, and an item whose ID cannot be read is skipped with a warning while the rest syncs normally (reported by foXaCe).

Fixed: changing Folder Mode, or moving a category to another folder, no longer leaves every moved item in your library twice. The old copies are removed even beyond the orphan safety limit, as long as the item only moved to another category folder; anything that actually disappeared is still protected by the limit. Moved items lose their watched status, because Jellyfin sees a new folder as a new item (reported in andreadegiovine's fork).

Fixed: when orphan cleanup removes a movie or series, the NFO and poster the plugin wrote are removed with it, so the folder no longer stays behind. Files you added yourself, such as subtitles or your own NFO, are kept, and so is the folder (idea from andreadegiovine).

Fixed: with "Group movies with the same TMDB id" on, a film whose request the provider missed no longer ends up in a folder of its own. It is held back and picked up on the next sync. Films already split this way stay split; to fix them, use Delete Movies Library in the Danger Zone and sync again (reported by andreadegiovine).

New: with "Fallback to Year-Free Lookup" on, an unmatched movie is also searched with the year of the provider's release date and with its original title, which helps when the title carries the wrong year or is in another language. A search without a year is checked against the release date, so it cannot pick a remake. A match found by the year-free retry is now remembered for later syncs, for movies and series. Movies already in your library keep their folders (idea from philx17).

New: "Publish Playlists" on the Live TV tab. The M3U and Catch-up M3U URLs contain your Xtream username and password and can be reached without a Jellyfin login. They are now only served while this switch is on, and it is off when you enable Live TV from now on. The EPG URL and channel logos are not affected (proposed by dillardblom).

New: "Restrict These URLs To" limits the Live TV URLs to the addresses you list, one per line. Leave it empty for no restriction. If you use it, include 127.0.0.1 and ::1, since Jellyfin fetches channel logos itself, and behind a reverse proxy add the proxy to Known Proxies in Jellyfin's networking settings first (written by dillardblom).

Fixed: a Live TV category, channel or logo address with & in it no longer shows as & or breaks (reported by TheBazeman).

This update brings together 1.55.1.0 to 1.55.3.0 from the beta channel.

Fixed: Request Delay now limits how fast the plugin talks to your provider in total. Each parallel worker used to apply it separately, so with Sync Parallelism at 10 and the default of 50 ms up to 200 requests a second could go out, enough for some providers to block your IP. It is now one shared gap per provider: 50 ms means at most 20 a second. When the provider says it is getting too many requests, every request to it waits. A first sync of a large library takes longer as a result; if your provider allows more, lower Request Delay. Setting it to 0 is no longer saved as 50 (reported by dillardblom).

Fixed: with "Group movies with the same TMDB id" on, a film whose request the provider missed no longer ends up in a folder of its own. It is held back and picked up on the next sync. Films already split this way stay split; to fix them, use Delete Movies Library in the Danger Zone and sync again (reported by andreadegiovine).

Fixed: a Live TV category, channel or logo address with & in it no longer shows as & or breaks (reported by TheBazeman).

Categories load their items again on Jellyfin 12 (#117).

Jellyfin 12 stops accepting the legacy `X-Emby-Token` request header. Two of the configuration page fetch sites still sent it: the Live TV category loader and the Series / VOD content loader. Both now send `Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=` instead, which Jellyfin 12's `CustomAuthentication` middleware expects. The Test connection button was never affected and still works as before. Two-line header swap in `config.js`, no server-side change.

Test Dispatcharr now tests the password you just typed.

Typing a Dispatcharr API password and pressing Test before saving tested the password that was already saved, not the one on screen. It came back red with "authentication failed" for credentials that were perfectly correct, and nothing suggested that saving first would change the answer. Type, test, save once it goes green is the obvious way to use a test button, and that order never worked.

It now sends what is on the form, the way the Test Connection button above it always has. Clearing the Dispatcharr URL and pressing Test now tests the Xtream address, which is what leaving that field empty means, instead of quietly putting the old URL back.

A provider you are setting up for the first time can be tested as well. Before, with nothing saved yet, it answered "Please configure Base URL first" about a Base URL sitting on screen in front of you.

Nothing else changed, and catch-up, syncing and Live TV are untouched.

The last of your provider password is out of the Live TV playlist.

1.53 replaced every stream URL in LiveTv.m3u and Catchup.m3u with a Dispatcharr address that needs no credentials. One thing still carried the password: the catch-up attribute on channels that have an archive. That attribute is a template your IPTV app fills in and plays by itself, so it has to work on its own, and the only address that does is the one with your username and password in it. Dispatcharr has a catch-up address of its own, but it refuses callers who have not logged in, and these playlists are deliberately served without a Jellyfin login so that Jellyfin's own tuner can read them. There was nothing safe to put there, so the attribute is now left out.

What this changes for you: nothing, if you watch catch-up in Jellyfin. Those channels still have their archive and still play the same way. If you point an external IPTV app at these playlists, that app will no longer offer catch-up on those channels. If you would rather have it back, there is a new setting under Catch-up / Timeshift that puts the attribute in again, with the warning that it carries your password.

Measured on a live setup before and after: 720 channels, 63 lines with the password in them, now none.

Also fixed: the line in the log that tells you how much of the playlist still carries credentials only appeared on the rare occasions the plugin fetched the channel list fresh. It now appears whenever a playlist is built, which is when you would actually go looking for it.

Your provider password is no longer in the Live TV playlist.

If you run Dispatcharr in front of your provider, the M3U the plugin serves now points at Dispatcharr's own channel addresses instead of building URLs with your Xtream username and password in them. Those URLs have always been reachable without a Jellyfin login, on purpose, because Jellyfin's own tuner cannot send one, which meant anyone who had one of those links also had your provider account. Measured on a real setup: 720 of 720 channels, every stream address credential free, where before every single line carried the password.

A channel Dispatcharr does not recognise keeps its old address rather than disappearing from your guide, and the log says how many did and that those lines still carry credentials. Without Dispatcharr nothing changes at all.

One part is not done yet. Channels with a catch-up archive carry a separate address for replaying past programmes, and that one is a template other apps fill in themselves, so it still has your credentials in it. On the setup this was measured against that is 63 lines out of 720. Finishing it needs checking how Dispatcharr expects a time to be expressed, which has not been verified, so it was left rather than guessed at.

Also fixed: with Dispatcharr on a different address than your provider, movie links were pointed at the wrong one of the two.

Channels that would not direct play, and quicker metadata behind Dispatcharr.

Fixed: if your provider does not send stream statistics, every channel arrived at your player with nothing to say what it actually was. Players refused them as an unsupported format, and the server re-encoded pictures they could have shown as they were, without graphics acceleration because it did not know what it was decoding either. Jellyfin can work this out by looking at the stream, and the plugin was accidentally stopping it from looking. Channels from providers that do send statistics are unchanged. One trade-off worth knowing: if the inspection fails, Jellyfin now assumes the picture is interlaced and smooths it, which is slower than before, where the plugin simply asserted it was not (diagnosed by pemontto).

Changed: with Dispatcharr Mode on, film and series descriptions, cast, ratings and artwork now come from Dispatcharr directly instead of going the long way round through its Xtream compatibility layer. Series episodes had no Dispatcharr route at all until now. Anything that does not answer falls back to the old route, so a Dispatcharr too old to have these endpoints keeps working exactly as before, and with Dispatcharr Mode off nothing changes at all (contributed by dillardblom).

Radio channels, and a plainer warning about the Live TV setup URLs.

Fixed: radio stations were published as ordinary television channels. Providers mark them with a stream type that the plugin read and then ignored, so they ended up in the TV list with everything else. The playlist now flags them as radio, which is what players like Kodi use to put them under Radio, and the built-in tuner reports them as radio to Jellyfin, which keeps radio in its own section. Only the one value that is known to mean radio counts: providers use that same field for their own bookkeeping, and guessing would move real television channels out of the TV list, which is harder to recover from than a radio station in the wrong place. If you run Dispatcharr in front of the plugin you will not see a difference, because it reports every channel as ordinary live TV (reported by dillardblom).

The three setup URLs on the Live TV tab now say what they are. They work without a Jellyfin login, on purpose, because Jellyfin's own tuner and guide fetcher do not send one when they fetch them. What was never spelled out is what that means: Xtream has no token or session, so your provider username and password sit in every stream line of the playlist, and anyone who can reach one of those URLs has your account. The settings page, the README and the developer notes now all say so, along with the two things that limit it: keeping those URLs off the open internet, and using the built-in tuner, which never publishes a playlist at all (raised by dillardblom).

Watch programmes that have already aired.

New: a Xtream Catch-up entry under Channels. Pick a channel, pick a day, and play something that has already been on. Jellyfin's own Live TV cannot do this at all: its player refuses any programme once its end time has passed, and there is no setting anywhere to change that. This sits beside Live TV rather than replacing it, so live viewing and recording keep working exactly as they do now.

It is off until you switch it on. You need Enable Catch-up, which you may already have on for other apps, plus the new Watch catch-up inside Jellyfin. Only channels your provider keeps an archive for appear, and only for as many days back as that provider actually keeps.

Some providers publish only what is coming and never what has been, so a day that has passed lists nothing even though the recording plays perfectly well. Those days are offered in blocks of time instead, so you pick half past eight on Saturday rather than a title. Channels that do publish a proper guide show programme names as you would expect.

Providers disagree about what time it is, and asking for the wrong hour would quietly give you the wrong programme with no error. The plugin now asks your provider what time it thinks it is and requests the recording for the hour it actually aired. If a provider answers that wrongly there is a correction setting under Catch-up.

Fixed: the catch-up day limit on the settings page refused anything above 14, while the server has always accepted up to 30 (raised by dillardblom in the same discussion).

Name your providers, a connection test that says what is actually wrong, and a settings page that stops breaking after you remove a provider.

New: providers can be given a name. The dropdown at the top of the settings page listed them as Provider 1, Provider 2 and so on, which tells you nothing once you have more than a couple of accounts configured. There is a Name field on the General tab now, and the list updates as you type. Leave it empty and it goes back to numbering them, so nothing changes if you do not use it (suggested by dillardblom).

Fixed: removing a provider could leave the Add Provider button dead, with nothing happening when you clicked it and a page refresh not helping. Moving around the Jellyfin dashboard rebuilds the settings page in place, and being rebuilt a second time made it fail before any of its buttons were connected (reported by dillardblom).

Fixed: Test Connection answered every bad address with the same sentence about needing http:// in front, even when the address on screen looked perfectly normal. It now shows the value it could not read, and tells you when the address you typed is not the address it would actually contact. That last one is the case you cannot see: an invisible character or a lookalike letter copied in from a provider's web page quietly turns the host into something else (reported by dillardblom).

Fixed: the Live TV instructions told you to add the playlist address as an HDHomeRun tuner, which does not work. It is an M3U Tuner. The three addresses under Setup URLs belong in three different places, one of which is not Jellyfin at all, and each line now says where it goes. The Xtream Library entry that appears in Jellyfin's own tuner list is explained as well (reported by dillardblom).

Also: the option that groups films sharing a TMDB id now says how to apply it to films already in your library, and what that costs you (raised by andreadegiovine).

Playback failures from a stray space, lost artwork on multi-version films, Dispatcharr logins, and two new grouping options.

Fixed: a password saved with a space before or after it was used exactly as typed, so every stream URL came out malformed and playback failed with a 403 on every single item; both password fields are now trimmed and configurations already saved are corrected too, so nothing needs re-entering (reported by jamillejh). Films your provider carries as V1, V2 and V3 all write to one information file, and they were written at the same time without coordination, so they could overwrite each other and a version whose details could not be fetched would replace a complete file with an empty one; this became visible in 1.47.0.0, which is what put real content in those files, and the version with actual information now wins whichever one finishes first (reported by andreadegiovine). Dispatcharr mode had no address of its own, so the login went to your Xtream server, which has no such page and answers "not found"; there is now a Dispatcharr URL field, and leaving it empty keeps the old behaviour of using the Xtream address (reported by jght2). New: an option to put the category in front of Live TV channel numbers, so a guide built from several categories stays grouped instead of interleaved, which also stops two channels sharing a number and one of them becoming unreachable (requested by dulfer). And a per-provider option to write copies of a film that your provider reports under the same TMDB id into one folder, so Jellyfin shows them as versions of one film; only ids your provider supplies are grouped, never ones found by searching on the title, so a film and its remake cannot be merged by accident (requested by andreadegiovine). Both new options are off by default and neither moves or renames anything already in your library. (#83, #84, #86, #88, #90)

Your movies and shows arrive with descriptions, cast and artwork.

Until now the plugin wrote almost nothing alongside each file it created: a title, a year and an ID. Anything Jellyfin's own metadata providers could not identify therefore sat in your library as a bare entry with no poster and no synopsis. Your provider was already sending the plot, genre, cast, director, country, rating, release date, trailer and poster and backdrop images, and the plugin was discarding all of it. That information is now written into the files Jellyfin reads. Posters and backdrops are referenced straight from your provider, so nothing extra is downloaded to your server. Anything Jellyfin can identify on its own is unaffected, its own metadata still takes priority, and any field your provider leaves empty is simply left out rather than written blank. Items also carry the date your provider added them, so Recently added reflects the provider's catalogue; providers report that date in two different formats and both are now understood. Contributed by @andreadegiovine. (#87)

Switching a provider back to Single folder mode keeps your category ticks.

If you had a provider set to Multiple folder mode and switched it back to Single, the category list came back with every box unticked, even though your categories were still configured. Saving from that screen wrote an empty selection, and an empty selection means "sync everything", so a setup meant to cover a handful of categories quietly pulled in the provider's entire catalogue. The list now comes back with the categories you had assigned to your folders already ticked.

This only affected configurations last saved on 1.44.0.0 or earlier. If you have saved your settings on 1.45.0.0 or later, you were never exposed to it.

Sync every Live TV channel except the categories you pick.

Live TV used to offer two choices: take every channel your provider has, or tick the categories you want one by one. The second option meant that whenever your provider added a new category, you silently missed it until you happened to notice and tick it. There is now a third option, "Sync all channels EXCEPT the categories you tick". Tick the handful you never watch and everything else comes through, including any category your provider adds later. Tick nothing and you get everything. Movies and Series already worked this way; Live TV now matches them. Per-channel exclusions work in the new mode too, so you can still drop individual channels from the categories you are keeping.

Saving the config page could wipe your Live TV category selection. If you opened the plugin settings and saved before the category list had finished loading, or without loading it at all, your selection was quietly replaced with an empty one. In the "pick specific channels" mode that meant no channels synced at all. Your saved selection is now left alone unless the list is actually on screen.

Live TV could fail to load channels on some providers. Providers report which categories a channel belongs to in several different formats, and anything other than the most common one caused the whole channel fetch to fail rather than just that one field, which could take out Live TV entirely. All the known formats are now accepted.

Multiple folder mode with no categories assigned now syncs nothing instead of everything.

IF YOU USE MULTIPLE FOLDER MODE, READ THIS. Previously, a provider set to Multiple folder mode with no categories assigned to any folder synced the provider's ENTIRE catalogue into the root of your library, because an empty selection was read as "no filter". It now syncs nothing and tells you why. If your sync suddenly does nothing after upgrading, that is this change: assign categories to your folders, or switch Folder Mode back to Single (which still means "sync everything"). Your existing files are not deleted - orphan cleanup refuses to run when the selection resolves to nothing.

Blocked orphan cleanup is no longer invisible. When cleanup is skipped because the deletion ratio exceeds the safety threshold, the sync used to report success with zero deletions and zero errors, identical to a healthy run. The counts are now on the sync result, the Last Sync panel shows them with a warning, and the run says so at the end instead of in a single log line thousands of entries earlier.

The config page refuses to save a Multiple folder mode provider with no categories assigned, and can no longer wipe a saved folder configuration when the category list has not loaded.

Known issue: switching folder mode from Multiple back to Single repaints the category list but does not restore the ticks, so check your selection before saving in that case. Tracked in issue #81.

Nearly all of this release comes from @andreadegiovine, who reported the problems, found the causes and wrote the code. BEFORE YOU UPDATE: movie folders carrying a version tag are renamed, so "Movie Name [V1]" becomes "Movie Name" and all versions of a film sit together. The old folders become orphans and are removed on your next sync if Clean up orphaned files is on, taking watched status and any artwork in them with it. If a large share of your library carries those tags the rename can exceed the Orphan Safety Threshold, in which case cleanup is skipped and you will see both old and new folders until you raise it. New: movie and series category pickers get an Include / Exclude selector, so you can tick the categories you do not want and have everything else sync, including categories your provider adds later. Duplicate copies of a film tagged V1, V2 and similar now group into one entry with a version dropdown instead of appearing as separate movies. The Orphan Safety Threshold is now editable in the plugin settings instead of only in the configuration file on the server. Fixed: when a provider offered the same film twice with the same quality tag, the second copy silently replaced the first with nothing logged and no error reported, and which copy survived could change between syncs. The same applied to episodes sharing a season and episode number. (#74, #76, #80)

Adds a per-provider Request Timeout setting under Performance. Providers with very large catalogs could not answer within the fixed 100 second limit, which failed the whole channel, movie or series fetch. Timeouts are now retried, and the error says the request timed out instead of reporting it as cancelled. Live TV also starts faster after a restart: the channel list is served from local storage while it refreshes in the background, instead of making Jellyfin wait for a full download from your provider. Also fixes release builds reporting the wrong version number under Dashboard > Plugins. (#73)
fix: repair incomplete series folders during incremental sync — verifies snapshot entries have actual .strm files before skipping them, preventing orphaned folders with only metadata (#65, fixes #64)
feat: multi-provider Live TV support — configure multiple Xtream providers simultaneously for Live TV channels (#63, closes #56)

Channel Overrides now accept an optional 4th field: StreamId=Name|Number|LogoUrl|Tags (comma-separated). Tags are applied to Live TV channels and can be used for Jellyfin access control (show/hide channels per user). See PR #61.

Fix duplicate series folders when TVDB/TMDB ID lookup fails (rate limited, timeout, or no match). The plugin now reuses the existing named folder instead of creating a duplicate with no identifier suffix.

Live TV channels are now grouped by their Xtream category. Each channel is tagged with its provider category, so the Jellyfin Live TV guide shows category groups instead of one flat list. Applies to native tuner (ChannelGroup) and M3U/XMLTV (group-title).
Channel Override logos can now be a local file path (e.g. /media/logos/fox.png), not just an http(s) URL. The plugin serves local logos over HTTP. Resolves #53.
Adds per-item selection for Movies and Series, matching Live TV per-channel selection. Expand a Movie or Series category to enable or disable individual titles. Resolves #54.

Adds an in-Jellyfin 'Use beta channel' toggle under Dashboard > Plugins > Xtream Library > Settings > General > Updates. When enabled, the plugin registers its beta plugin manifest URL with Jellyfin's plugin repository list so pre-release versions appear in Dashboard > Plugins > Catalog like any other plugin. Disabling removes the entry. State persists across Jellyfin restarts. This release also rolls up everything previously available only on the beta channel between v1.34.0.0 and v1.36.6.0: multi-provider config UI improvements (#36), live-stream date parsing fixes (#41), three EPG XMLTV parsing bugs (#45), legacy-config recovery for users orphaned by the v1.33.3.0 GUID change (#49), Native Tuner UI duplicate-channel warning (#50), multi-provider Live TV URL construction fix (#46), and Live TV channel counts on the sync status dashboard (#48). See https://github.com/firestaerter3/Jellyfin-Xtream-Library/releases for full per-version notes.

Adds a direct 'Xtream Library' entry to the Jellyfin admin dashboard sidebar (#36, thanks @dwizzle204). Sets EnableInMainMenu = true on the embedded config page so the sidebar surfaces an Xtream Library entry directly under Dashboard > Plugins, alongside the existing Dashboard > Plugins > Xtream Library path. Pure UX improvement, no functional change. Cherry-picked from the original PR with author credit preserved via Co-Authored-By, the original PR's new PluginTests.cs collided with the unrelated test file added for BUG-009, so the sidebar-registration assertion is now an additional test on the existing PluginTests.cs.

Fixes live-stream list fetch failures on Xtream providers that return the 'added' field as a formatted date string (e.g. '22/05/2024 10:00:00') instead of a Unix timestamp (#41, thanks @gamegninou). LiveStreamInfo.Added was previously typed as long, which forced strict integer JSON deserialization and threw JsonSerializationException for the entire live-stream list whenever the provider used the string variant. The field has zero readers in the codebase, it only exists for round-trip JSON purposes, so the loosest type that accepts every provider variant is right. Changed to string, matching the sibling StreamInfo.Added (VOD movies) which has always been a string. Intentionally simpler than the converter-based approach proposed in #41, which tried MM/dd before dd/MM and would have silently mis-parsed ambiguous dates with day ≤ 12. 4 new deserialization tests.

Recovers configuration for users who lost their plugin settings across the v1.33.3.0 GUID change (#49). Some users who upgraded from v1.31.44.0 (the [MOVED] shim) to v1.33.3.0+ (the new GUID build) ended up with their pre-v1.32 settings (BaseUrl, folder mappings, etc.) orphaned in a sibling XML file while the new plugin started against an empty in-memory config. The existing migration only operated on what Jellyfin had already loaded, so the orphan was never recovered. This release adds a constructor-time importer that runs before the existing migration: when the in-memory config looks completely fresh, scan the configurations directory for two known historical config filenames our plugin has ever written, validate each candidate against a schema sentinel (folder mappings or TMDb/TVDb override maps populated) that distinguishes our schema from the upstream Kevin Jilissen Jellyfin.Xtream plugin's, copy the legacy fields in, and rename the chosen orphan to .migrated-<date>.bak so it is not picked up on next boot. Defensive: strict trigger gate (only fires when Providers is empty AND BaseUrl is empty AND folder mappings are empty); schema sentinel prevents credential cross-pollination if both plugins are installed side-by-side; orphan is renamed not deleted, preserving an audit copy; rename failure is non-fatal because the import already succeeded in memory. Third installment of the multi-provider migration story (v1.33.1.0 fixed endpoint gating, v1.33.2.0 fixed the pre-v1.32 startup migration, v1.36.1.0 fixed URL construction, this fixes the case where the migration target file is not the file the user's data is in). No configuration change required.

Fixes three distinct EPG parsing bugs (#45, thanks @FilipBB). (1) XmlReader double-advance: AppendUpstreamProgrammes used XNode.ReadFrom inside a while(reader.Read()) loop, which advances the reader twice per element. For minified XMLTV (no whitespace between programme tags) every other programme was silently skipped from the guide. (2) Offset parsing failure on +HH:MM style offsets: TryParseXmltvTime only accepted +HHMM. Modern XMLTV providers that use the ISO 8601 style with a colon (e.g. +02:00) had their programmes parsed as UTC and filtered out as in-the-past. (3) Aggressive past-filter dropped currently-playing shows: any programme ending even a second before now was discarded, so minor clock skew between provider and server made the now-playing show disappear from the guide. Now: 1-hour grace period. Also: extra date format support (YYYYMMDDHHMM and YYYYMMDD as accepted alternatives) and 7 new tests covering offset forms and short date formats. Follow-up marks TryParseXmltvTime as internal so the tests can call it directly instead of via reflection.

Clarifies the Enable Native Tuner UI to prevent duplicate Live TV channels (#50). The previous checkbox description told users to add the Xtream Library tuner manually under Dashboard > Live TV > Tuner Devices, but Jellyfin does not show ITunerHost-based tuners there (that list is only for manually-added tuners). Users who followed the instruction and also pasted the M3U URL as a manual HDHomeRun tuner ended up with both code paths publishing the same channel set, hence every channel appearing twice in the guide. This release replaces the misleading instruction with an accurate one, adds a 'Pick one tuner mode' warning inline under the Native Tuner checkbox explicitly calling out the duplicate-channels symptom, notes the transcoding-vs-remux trade-off so users can choose the right mode for their hardware, and adds a matching warning in the Setup URLs section so the cross-reference is visible from either entry point. No tuner code change; both modes remain fully supported.

Fixes Live TV playback on multi-provider configs (#46 follow-up). Users who configured their provider exclusively via the multi-provider UI (introduced in v1.32) were getting unplayable channels because the M3U export and native tuner both emitted stream URLs shaped like /live///{streamId}.ts — no scheme, no server, no credentials. FFmpeg refused with 'No such file or directory'. Cause: BuildStreamUrl and BuildCatchupUrl were the last consumers still reading the legacy single-provider config fields directly; on a fresh v1.32+ install those fields are empty and only Providers[0] is populated. Fix: a new ResolveLiveTvProvider helper resolves credentials from Providers[0] first (falling back to legacy fields for any config caught mid-migration), and all three URL builders route through it. Third installment of the multi-provider migration story (v1.33.1.0 fixed endpoint gating, v1.33.2.0 fixed the pre-v1.32 startup migration, this fixes URL construction). No configuration change required.

Live TV channel counts on the sync status dashboard (#48). After each sync, the dashboard panel now shows a Live TV row with the total channel count and added/updated/deleted split, matching the existing Movies and Series rows. The same counters appear in the live progress display while a sync is running. How it works: at the end of SyncAsync the plugin fetches the current channel set, compares it against a persisted JSON snapshot (live-tv-channels.json in the plugin data folder), and writes the new snapshot back. A channel counts as 'updated' when its name, EPG channel id, logo URL, or channel number differs. The M3U/EPG cache is invalidated as part of the refresh so Jellyfin's next tuner poll sees the new data. A Live TV refresh failure no longer aborts the sync — VOD/Series counts persist and the error message is surfaced separately. First sync after upgrade shows every channel as 'added' because no previous snapshot exists yet.

Live TV channel checkboxes track parent category state (#46 follow-up). After clicking the master Deselect All button in Pick mode, expanding any (now-deselected) category showed every channel underneath as ticked, even though those channels would not actually sync. Cause: per-channel checkbox state was computed purely from the excludedLiveStreamIds list, and v1.35.0.0's correct decision to clear that list on master Deselect All collapsed the rendering logic to 'all channels checked because nothing is excluded'. Fix: channel checkboxes now gate on the parent category checkbox as well, render unchecked with an italic hint when the parent is deselected, auto-tick the parent when the user re-enables an individual channel or panel-level Select All, and re-render any expanded child panel immediately when the category checkbox flips. No configuration change required.

Truncate STRM filenames to 255 bytes (fixes #47). Series with very long episode titles (e.g. one Interspecies Reviewers episode whose provider-supplied title runs to 240+ characters) silently failed to sync because the resulting STRM filename exceeded Linux's NAME_MAX per-component cap, throwing PathTooLongException on every sync attempt. The episode and movie filename builders now run their output through a UTF-8 byte-aware truncation step that preserves the .strm extension, respects multi-byte character boundaries (Japanese, emoji, etc.), and trims trailing separator punctuation introduced by the cut. 255 bytes is the cross-platform safe ceiling — Windows NTFS and macOS APFS use 255 UTF-16 code units which is laxer. No configuration change required.

Live TV channel selection overhaul (fixes #46). Three intertwined bugs are fixed: (1) category-level Deselect All now actually drops per-channel exclusions; (2) empty category selection no longer means 'sync all' — there is now an explicit Sync ALL vs Pick specific channels mode toggle; (3) new top-of-list toolbar (Select all / Deselect all / Clear channel exclusions), live counter, and client-side category search make handpicking a small subset fast. Existing configs with populated Live TV selections are auto-migrated to Custom mode to preserve behavior. Fresh installs stay on Sync ALL by default. Heads-up: configs with channel exclusions but no category selection land on Custom + empty selection (= zero channels) — click 'Select all' if that is not what you want.

Preserve full EPG metadata from upstream XMLTV (fixes #42): the plugin previously generated XMLTV from Xtream's JSON endpoint which only exposes title and description. It now passes the upstream xmltv.php through verbatim, preserving categories, ratings, credits, icons, dates, and star-ratings. Jellyfin can again categorize Live TV programs by genre. Falls back to the old JSON-based fetch if the upstream XMLTV is unavailable.

Fix overlapping plugin GUID (#43): the boilerplate placeholder GUID a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890 was shared with three unrelated Jellyfin plugins. Replaced with a freshly-generated random GUID. NOTE: existing installs are treated as a different plugin after upgrade — uninstall the old 'Xtream Library' entry from Jellyfin and reinstall to pick up this version. Plugin configuration is preserved across the reinstall. This release also rolls up multi-provider support (v1.32.0.0), per-channel Live TV selection (v1.33.0.0), and Live TV / legacy-config migration fixes (v1.33.1.0, v1.33.2.0) from the beta channel.

name: QualityGate [✓]
overview: Cap the resolution a user may be served, measured against the media's actual height.
description:
Quality Gate lets Jellyfin administrators cap the resolution a user may be served. The cap is measured against the media's actual height, read from its video stream, so it holds whatever the file is called. Media above the cap is served as a capped transcode, or as a lower-resolution version of the same item where one exists, and requests for the original file are refused. Useful for bandwidth management and tiered access.

versions.changelog:
- Administrators can now copy central groups into their own personal collection when switching back to personal mode, or import them later. Both management screens require an explicit copy/skip choice on mode switch. Existing personal groups take precedence when IDs match; central groups and other users' personal groups remain untouched. Custom group images are copied with newly imported groups.
- Require administrators to explicitly choose whether to copy their personal groups when switching to central management. The no-copy choice preserves personal groups for later use, and both the web dialog and plugin dashboard offer a later import. Reject an ambiguous mode-switch request instead of silently showing an empty central group list.

- Support Wholphin in the native Live TV guide: select a group or **All channels** directly in its compatible Control Center folders, then open **Live TV → TV Guide**. Group selection applies only to the authenticated user's device, respects current group/channel permissions, and restores the full guide on reset. Wholphin does not support an automatic guide jump.
- Add administrator switches for the official Jellyfin Android TV / Fire TV app and Wholphin. A sole eligible TV is selected automatically; with several TVs, the last available choice is remembered per user. Disabled or disconnected devices cannot receive playback or guide changes.
- Add recognizable artwork to the Control Center home tile, guide actions, confirmation and fallback folders. **All channels** has its own EPG-reset image; created groups have a distinct group image. Personal and shared groups can use custom PNG, JPEG or WebP images up to 5 MiB, with preview and reset controls and permission checks.
- Add recording controls to the grouped web EPG. Users with Jellyfin's Live TV management permission can schedule, edit and cancel single-program or series timers, including padding and series options; recording errors remain visible in the dialog.
- Restore reliable loading of the independent web EPG behind reverse proxies that cached its old script URL. Preserve original channel logos, official Android TV / Fire TV behavior, channel playback and the existing plugin identity and settings.

- Selecting a group in the official Android TV / Fire TV app immediately applies that group's native guide scope and opens the ordinary Live TV view. The separate Native TV guide action remains available to retry.
- Hide direct grouped-channel media tiles from that authenticated TV response while keeping the native guide action and browsable program-list fallback. Internal channel items and playlists remain unchanged.
- Retain per-user/device validation, group access checks and safe behavior when navigation is unavailable. The original app may still require selecting TV Guide after opening Live TV; a direct timeline deep link is not exposed by the stock client.

- Organize Live TV channels in ordered personal groups independent of IPTV-provider categories, or use administrator-managed shared groups with per-group user access.
- Show one selected group's original channels in Jellyfin's native Android TV / Fire TV timeline. Select the group on the TV or from the web/mobile page; the web page can also apply the deduplicated union of all visible groups. Reset to all ordinarily permitted channels at any time. Selections are per user and TV device.
- Browse an independent web EPG with a channel/program timeline, now/next/later programs, channel cards, day/time navigation and zoom. Save visible/default groups and view preferences; use the interface in English or German.
- Use the web or phone guide as a remote for the official Jellyfin Android TV / Fire TV app: discover a compatible TV, remember the target, and start or switch live channels while the guide stays open.
- Apply optional central channel-access rules to selected users, including children's accounts. Restrictions cover the plugin and ordinary Jellyfin Live TV, direct playback, playlists and associated recordings while preserving Jellyfin permissions.
- Browse grouped channel and daily program folders in supported native apps; optionally mirror groups as playlists for other clients.
- Integrate the web interface through File Transformation, optionally add a Plugin Pages menu shortcut, customize the display name and hide the original Live TV home tile when the groups entry is available.
- Support Jellyfin 12.0 or later in the Jellyfin 12 series (12.1 confirmed). Keep the existing plugin ID, channel identity and stored settings for upgrades from Live-TV Groups. Native guide navigation may require one additional TV Guide selection; no virtual channels or custom TV client are used.

name: Marquee Companion [✓✓]
description:
Adds four independent capabilities: server-side filtering by media-stream characteristics that Jellyfin's core API can't express (video dynamic range, codecs, audio channel count, and spatial audio), plus opt-in global recent-podcast discovery via Podcast Index using administrator-provided credentials, plus opt-in passwordless sign-in by emailed magic link over administrator-configured SMTP, plus an opt-in scheduled task that recovers the release date of items that arrived without one by reading it from the file name. The filtering API exposes a paginated, BaseItemDto-compatible endpoint and a capability endpoint for client feature-detection.

versions.changelog:
- Initial release. - Resolution (isHd/is4K) passthrough for client filtering. - Fix: filtering by a library returned no items. The library (parentId) is now
  resolved into its contents so video range / codec / audio filters work when
  scoped to a specific library.
- Renamed the plugin to "Marquee Companion" (display name only; API route,
  plugin id, and behavior unchanged).
- Capabilities are now scoped to the requested library (parentId): the available
  values offered for a library are drawn only from items in that library, so any
  single facet selection is guaranteed to match at least one item there. Omitting
  parentId still returns the global value set.
- TV libraries now filter correctly by stream facets. Stream attributes live on
  episodes, but TV libraries are browsed at the series level; the filter now
  matches episodes and returns the shows that have at least one matching episode.
  Also forces a recursive query so a library id resolves to its contents.
- Added opt-in recent podcast discovery through Podcast Index. - Podcast discovery now logs why it returned nothing. The endpoint still answers 404 for
  every failure, but the server log distinguishes disabled credentials, a Podcast Index
  rejection, and feeds dropped during validation — including a per-rule tally of what was
  dropped.
- Removes the YouTube trailer resolver. Clients now hand YouTube trailers to the YouTube
  app instead, so the server no longer downloads, verifies, updates, or executes yt-dlp or a
  JavaScript runtime.
- Removes the yt-dlp and JavaScript-runtime downloads earlier versions installed. Those
  binaries are unreachable now the resolver is gone, so the plugin reclaims the directory it
  created rather than leaving an administrator to find it. Only its own install root is
  touched, and a failure to delete never stops the plugin starting.
- Fix: Podcast Discovery always returned 404 when enabled. Podcast Index sends the envelope's
  `status` as a JSON boolean, but it was bound to a string, so the whole recent-feeds payload
  failed to deserialize. Both the boolean and the documented string form are now accepted, and
  an unusable payload is logged with the value exactly as it arrived.
- Added opt-in email sign-in. A client posts an email address, the server mails a single-use
  link, and confirming that link signs the waiting device in — no password, and no typing on a
  TV remote. The email can be opened on any device, so it works for tvOS; when it is opened on
  the signing-in device itself, the confirmation page also offers a deep link straight back into
  the app. Unrecognised addresses can optionally register, in which case the new account is
  created disabled and copies an administrator-chosen template user's permissions, so nothing is
  accessible until an administrator enables it. SMTP host, port, security, credentials and
  from-address are configured in the plugin settings, along with link lifetime and rate limits;
  a "send test email" button reports the mail server's own error when submission fails. The
  endpoint reports an explicit error rather than a silent success when SMTP is not configured.
- Fix: an audio filter matched files that had each thing you asked for, but never in
  the same track. Asking for AC-3 in 5.1 returned 444 movies on a test library, of which
  only 247 had an AC-3 track that was itself 5.1 — the rest were "DTS 5.1 main track plus
  AC-3 2.0 commentary" files that answered "has AC-3" and "has six channels" separately.
  Codec, channel count and spatial format are now read per audio track and have to hold on
  ONE of them. A filter naming a single audio facet is unaffected. The values offered by
  /Capabilities are unchanged.
- Music libraries can now be filtered by codec and channel count. Tracks were never
  catalogued, so every audio filter over a music library returned nothing at all while the
  same library unfiltered returned 11,022 tracks.
- Release-date recovery reads the FILE NAME first and falls back to date added, and
  understands two-digit-year release names (Name.25.02.05.Title). Date added is when a
  file reached the server, not when it was released: on a 650-item dry run, leading with
  it produced 18 distinct dates with 605 identical, while the name gave 98 spanning 2013
  to 2026.
- Release-date recovery is chosen PER LIBRARY. - Added opt-in release-date recovery. Downloaded YouTube content carries its upload
  date only in the file name, so Jellyfin stores no premiere date and reads the leading
  YYYYMMDD as a production year like 20250823 — those items then cannot appear in any
  view ordered by release date, on any client. A new scheduled task, "Recover missing
  release dates", reads the date from the production-year stamp, an sYYYY.eMMDDnn name,
  or a bare YYYYMMDD run, and writes it along with the corrected year. Off by default,
  previews to the log until an administrator turns preview off, and never modifies an
  item that already has a release date.
- Adds the seamless Marquee Companion panel to Jellyfin Web without manual web-client changes. - Adds paired Jellyfin 10/.NET 9 and Jellyfin 12/.NET 10 package builds.

versions.changelog:
## v1.7.1.0
### New
- Redesigned settings page.
- New "Remove plain lyrics that hide synced lyrics" option, on by default. Turn it off if other apps use the lyrics files in your music folder.
### Fixes
- Synced lyrics now show up even when a plain .txt sits next to the song. Before, Jellyfin kept showing the plain lyrics and the task re-downloaded the synced ones every run. -> #59

## v1.7.1.0
### New
- Redesigned settings page.
- New "Remove plain lyrics that hide synced lyrics" option, on by default. Turn it off if other apps use the lyrics files in your music folder.
### Fixes
- Synced lyrics now show up even when a plain .txt sits next to the song. Before, Jellyfin kept showing the plain lyrics and the task re-downloaded the synced ones every run. -> #59

## v1.7.0.0
### New
- Jellyfin 12 support. Every release now ships two builds, one for Jellyfin 12 and one for Jellyfin 10.11, and Jellyfin installs the right one for your server automatically.
- Jellyfin 10.11.0 and newer are supported again. The previous release required at least 10.11.6.
- New "Disable rate limiting" option for self-hosted LRCLIB servers. It removes the delay between requests, which speeds up large libraries. Requests to the public lrclib.net stay rate limited.
### Fixes
- Tracks that only have an album artist tag (compilations, classical music, many rips) now get lyrics. Strict search used to give up without an artist tag, and fuzzy search ignored the album artist entirely.
- Fuzzy search now tries every artist tagged on a track instead of only the first one.
- A system clock jump (NTP correction, VM resume) can no longer stall lyric requests.

## v1.7.0.0
### New
- Jellyfin 12 support. Every release now ships two builds, one for Jellyfin 12 and one for Jellyfin 10.11, and Jellyfin installs the right one for your server automatically.
- Jellyfin 10.11.0 and newer are supported again. The previous release required at least 10.11.6.
- New "Disable rate limiting" option for self-hosted LRCLIB servers. It removes the delay between requests, which speeds up large libraries. Requests to the public lrclib.net stay rate limited.
### Fixes
- Tracks that only have an album artist tag (compilations, classical music, many rips) now get lyrics. Strict search used to give up without an artist tag, and fuzzy search ignored the album artist entirely.
- Fuzzy search now tries every artist tagged on a track instead of only the first one.
- A system clock jump (NTP correction, VM resume) can no longer stall lyric requests.

## v1.6.6.0
### Fixes
- The lyrics task no longer re-downloads tracks that already have synced lyrics on disk. When a track's lyrics were saved but the database still reported them as plain (Jellyfin doesn't refresh metadata after a download until the next library scan), the task kept "upgrading" the same tracks on every run. It now trusts the synced .lrc file already on disk and skips it. -> #43

## v1.6.5.0
### Fixes
- Build against Jellyfin 10.11.6 instead of always the latest release. Previous builds were linked against 10.11.10 assemblies, which made Jellyfin report the plugin as "not supported" (TypeLoadException) on older 10.11.x servers. The plugin is now compatible with Jellyfin 10.11.6 and newer. -> #55

## v1.6.4.0
### Fixes
- Lyric file detection now also checks Jellyfin's internal metadata folder, not just the media folder. With "Save lyrics into media folders" disabled, already-downloaded lyrics are detected instead of being re-downloaded on every task run, which also reduces load on lrclib.net -> #54

## v1.6.3.0
### What's New
- Optional self-hosted LRCLIB server URL: point the plugin at your own LRCLIB instance instead of lrclib.net. Subpath URLs are preserved and the URL is validated on save. Thanks to @Nausi-llon (#50).
- Built-in rate limiting for lrclib.net requests: enforces a 200 ms minimum gap between calls and honors HTTP 429 `Retry-After` so transient spikes back off cleanly instead of surfacing as per-track errors.
- Identifiable User-Agent on every lrclib request (`jellyfin-plugin-lyrics/<version> (+repo-url)`) so the LRCLIB operators can distinguish this plugin from `jellyfin/jellyfin-plugin-lrclib` (#49).

### Notes
- No configuration changes required for existing users — the self-host URL defaults to `https://lrclib.net` and the rate limit only kicks in under load.

## v1.6.2.0
### What's New
- Auto-removes the official "LrcLib Lyrics" plugin (`jellyfin-plugin-lrclib`) on startup if installed, since both plugins register the same lyrics provider and conflict. This plugin is a fork that fixes critical issues — see README. The old plugin can be reinstalled later to switch back.

## v1.6.1.0
### What's New
- Lyrics alternative discovery: skip re-downloading lyrics that already failed in a previous run
- Synced-lyric upgrade now checks the existing sidecar file before replacing plain text

### Fixes
- Stop matching instrumental tracks against unrelated songs: honor LRCLIB's instrumental flag, validate every match against requested duration and artist, and drop the track-name-only fuzzy fallback when artist info is available (#40)
- Scheduled task log: split DB-desync skips from "already synced" skips so plain `.txt` sidecars are no longer counted as synced

### Settings
- New configurable duration-tolerance filter (default on, ±15s) with UI toggle to tune or disable

### Notes
- Jellyfin 10.11.6 or newer is now recommended (see README)

## v1.6.0.0
### What's New
- Added song title cleanup to strip YouTube-style suffixes (Official Music Video, etc.) and duplicate artist names
- Added progressive search fallback: retries with fewer parameters when no results are found
- Added multi-artist support: splits "artist1/artist2" and tries each artist individually
- Replace non-synced lyrics with synced ones when available
- Sped up scheduled lyrics task

### Fixes
- Fixed DI issue with RetryStateStore causing plugin to malfunction on startup
- Fixed fuzzy search failing when album name is missing
- Fixed crash on missing artist or invalid id

### Defaults Changed
- Strict search is now disabled by default
- "Exclude album name" is now enabled by default

## v1.5.0.0
### What's New
- Fixed support for Jellyfin 10.11

## v1.4.0.0
### What's New
- Added support for Jellyfin 10.11

## v1.3.0.0
### What's New
- Fixed a lot of plugin loading issues
- Fixed GitHub Action Workflows

### Technical Improvements
- Consistent versioning across all project files
- Better package compatibility with Jellyfin 10.9.x series
- Improved documentation and installation instructions

description:
Skip sponsored segments in YouTube videos using SponsorBlock data.

versions.changelog: Add an opt-in Jellyfin metadata source for YouTube IDs. Preserve filename and custom-regex matching as the default, read validated Youtube provider IDs imported from NFO uniqueid metadata, and expose the source choice in plugin settings.

Add Jellyfin 12 support. Retarget to .NET 10 and Jellyfin Controller 12.0.0-rc3, implement the new media-segment cleanup contract, and preserve the event-driven SponsorBlock workflow without enabling the core library segment scan.
Serialize SponsorBlock processing to avoid concurrent refresh and playback work for the same item. Bump the plugin version for local installation.

Add Done state with convergence-based polling. Videos older than 30 days (by YouTube publish date) are fetched once and frozen. Videos younger than 30 days are polled daily until segment data is unchanged for 5 consecutive checks, then frozen. Stale segments are now deleted when SponsorBlock data disappears. Daily scan task refactored to a clean two-phase dispatcher.

Add dedicated SponsorBlock log file (log_SponsorBlock_YYYYMMDD.log) in Jellyfin's log directory. All info/warning/error events now write to both the main server log and the dedicated file, so the plugin appears as a separate log entry in the Jellyfin dashboard.

Add comprehensive logging to the orchestrator and triggers. Every decision point (scope check, path empty, ID extraction failure, state-machine skip, segment write, state transition) now logs at information or debug level, so issues are diagnosable directly from the Jellyfin log dashboard.
Fix EnumerateScoped to discover Episode and Movie items, not just standalone Video. YouTube libraries imported as TV Shows store items as Episode type, which BaseItemKind.Video did not match.

Fix automatic loading for old archives and restore DLL-only release packaging. The daily refresh now discovers selected-library videos older than the sanity-check window, old untracked items use their Jellyfin DateCreated for the 48-hour decision, and NoData rows recheck after cooldown instead of being terminal.

Add a one-shot Force Scan button for existing archives. Admins can backfill every video in the selected libraries once, while the normal daily refresh stays limited to tracked Pending and HasData items. Includes duplicate-scan protection and status endpoints.

Repair pruned SponsorBlock segments on playback. When Jellyfin refreshes a changed media file it can delete generated MediaSegment rows while the plugin state still says HasData; playback start now verifies that Jellyfin still has segment rows and re-fetches/recreates them if they were pruned.

Fix delayed SponsorBlock loading. Register the daily refresh scheduled task so Pending items are retried automatically, correct the 24-hour playback retry condition, and wait for playback-start processing so freshly fetched segments can reach the first playback session.

Actually fix segments not reaching clients. Jellyfin's IMediaSegmentManager.CreateSegmentAsync expects the second arg to be the MD5-derived provider id (new Guid(MD5(name.ToLowerInvariant() UTF-16 LE)).ToString("N")), not the literal provider name. We were passing "SponsorBlock" verbatim, so stored segments didn't match any registered provider and the public MediaSegments API filtered them out. Pre-compute the hash and pass that. After upgrading, hit Reset on the config page so old segments get re-fetched under the correct provider id.

Fix segments not reaching clients. v1.1.0.0 dropped the IMediaSegmentProvider registration to avoid the slow scan, but Jellyfin filters segments by registered provider, so stored segments were never served. Re-register a stub provider (Supports => false, GetMediaSegments => empty) so Jellyfin recognizes 'SponsorBlock' as a known provider while the orchestrator stays in charge of fetching.

Add admin Reset button on the plugin config page that wipes SponsorBlock state and owned segments for items in the configured library scope, so the orchestrator re-fetches on next playback. Useful for re-fetching items whose SponsorBlock data became available after the initial scan.

Replace media-segment scan with event-driven orchestrator. Add daily refresh task at configurable hour. Add per-library scoping (empty by default — admin must opt in). SQLite per-item state machine (Pending/HasData/NoData) with 48h sanity check.
Remove non-functional user segment actions table from config page.
Initial release.

description:
Titoli, trame, generi, cast ed episodi degli anime in italiano da AnimeClick.it, completati da AniList, TMDB, TheTVDB e Fanart. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

Github: https://github.com/iCosiSenpai/jellyfin-plugin-animeclick
overview: Metadati anime in italiano da AnimeClick.it, con setup guidato, vetrina, libreria a locandine e una comunità che condivide le correzioni degli abbinamenti. Solo per Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

versions.changelog: Corretto il doppio caricamento dopo un aggiornamento (issue #2): lo ZIP contiene un meta.json con il nome del plugin, così Jellyfin tiene tutte le versioni sotto lo stesso nome e rimuove la vecchia, e all'avvio il plugin segna come superate le proprie copie più vecchie. Licenza AGPLv3 con termini aggiuntivi (attribuzione, versioni modificate riconoscibili, marchi e mascotte); attribuzione e link al codice sorgente nella pagina del plugin. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

AniList come fonte senza chiave insieme a TMDB: cast giapponese con i personaggi, studio di animazione, date, stato, voto, trailer, copertina e banner, solo nei campi vuoti. L'anno di una stagione senza date arriva dalla catena dei sequel di AniList, se gli episodi coincidono. Gli ID AniList che non corrispondono per tipo o anno vengono ignorati. Nuovo passo AniList nel setup. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

Comunità per tutti: dopo una correzione il plugin chiede se condividerla e la invia tramite il servizio della comunità, senza account; il token GitHub diventa facoltativo. Si condividono anche le stagioni con una scheda propria, applicate agli altri solo se numero di stagione ed episodi coincidono. Elenco approvato aggiornato ogni giorno, controlli automatici e approvazione con un'etichetta, tessera Comunità in Inizio, passo Comunità nel setup e scelta della stagione in «Correggi un abbinamento». Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

Pagina del plugin rifatta da zero con l'identità di AnimeClick: setup guidato al primo avvio e solo i passi nuovi dopo gli aggiornamenti importanti, vetrina degli ultimi anime aggiornati, cruscotto della collezione, libreria a locandine con titoli e trame uniti per anime, attivazione delle librerie a un clic e ricerca della scheda su AnimeClick per correggere un abbinamento. Corretti i conteggi dell'analisi di una singola serie, lo stato della condivisione comunitaria appena attivata e «Da verificare», che ora coincide con quanto «Sistema tutti i titoli» ricontrolla. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

Scarta i titoli alternativi di un'altra stagione verificando il titolo inglese originale. Quando manca una fonte coerente, traduce il titolo inglese già valido; esclude i nomi dei file. Correzione trovata sul NAS in anteprima, senza salvare la proposta errata. Include le novità 1.2.1. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

AnimeClick come unico provider remoto per le librerie anime: identificazione TMDB verificata, completamento dei metadati senza altri plugin e immagini integrate Fanart → TMDB → AnimeClick. Chiavi Fanart personale e di progetto nelle impostazioni, con link e verifica. Numerazione, campi bloccati e immagini esistenti conservati. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

AnimeClick primo campo per campo: i valori generici lasciano spazio alle fonti configurate. Recupero italiano e traduzione dall’inglese anche per serie, film, generi e tag, senza mescolare titolo e trama. Le immagini conservano la precedenza dei provider ad alta risoluzione; nessun aggiornamento immagini o riparazione viene avviato dall’installazione. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

Titoli episodio mancanti: ricerca su TheTVDB e TMDB configurati dopo AnimeClick, precedenza all’italiano e traduzione dei soli titoli inglesi con il profilo AI esistente. Verifica degli ID esterni, conservazione dei titoli compilati e indicazione della fonte nell’avanzamento. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

La tua libreria con analisi automatica, viste separate, avanzamento reale e interruzione dei lavori. Recupero dei soli titoli mancanti con protezione dei metadati esistenti. Abbinamenti della comunità e invio automatico delle correzioni su GitHub, entrambi facoltativi e disattivati di default. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

Major per Jellyfin 12 e .NET 10, verificata su 12.0 e 12.1. Interfaccia riprogettata con guida iniziale, preferenze semplici e strumenti avanzati separati. Identificazione automatica più prudente fra titoli simili, remake e stagioni; correzione manuale cercando il titolo in libreria e incollando il link AnimeClick, senza cancellazione diretta delle immagini. Corretti redirect di rete, collisioni e scadenza della cache, concorrenza nei refresh, rate limit e coerenza della coda traduzioni. AI opzionale e disattivabile senza perdere il profilo; impostazioni e credenziali esistenti conservate. 210 test backend per versione server e 11 test browser. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo: non installare su 10.11; le release precedenti restano disponibili. Dettagli e limiti delle verifiche nel rapporto di audit della release.

Ogni stagione riceve le sue sigle tramite i seguiti di AniList, i file portano il titolo del brano, e una pagina nel pannello mostra e controlla ogni abbinamento. Richiede Jellyfin 12.

versions.changelog: Versione per Jellyfin 12, con un'interfaccia nuova scritta da zero: libreria, pagina dell'anime con una scheda per stagione, mappa degli episodi, anteprima e scelta delle singole sigle, abbinamento manuale, attività, impostazioni e primo avvio guidato, più il pulsante nelle pagine degli anime. Ogni stagione riceve le sue sigle tramite i seguiti di AniList, solo quando anno ed episodi coincidono. I file prendono il titolo del brano e quelli della 1.x vengono rinominati, non riscaricati; le copie theme.mp3 duplicate vengono tolte. Corretti la sincronizzazione che ignorava gli abbinamenti manuali, il refresh completo dei metadati dopo ogni download, la sincronizzazione interrotta da un errore di rete, i tentativi infiniti sugli anime non trovati e i file cancellati a vicenda. Tolti playlist .m3u, prova a secco, preset e visualizzatore dei log. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

name: Mind the Gaps [✓]
description:
Scans your library for gaps (missing movies in partially-owned collections and franchises, missing series content, unowned titles from actor and director filmographies, and related recommendations) using TMDB, Trakt, TheTVDB, and TVmaze, with music and book sources (MusicBrainz, OpenLibrary, Discogs), and reads the watchlists and want-lists you already keep on those sites. Presents an easy todo list for filling out your collection, diagnoses why a title is reported missing, surfaces where to watch each item, and can optionally mint native virtual placeholders for missing items.

versions.changelog: 10.11.11.0 - Want to watch gains three options, all off by default and all requiring the arrived-titles playlist (contributed by David Rappo, @rappo, in PR 21): the home row can lead with the titles already on your playlist, a title comes off the playlist once it is watched (a series once every episode is played), and a movie or series page gets a bookmark button among its own. Plugin rows are reachable with a TV remote's D-pad. Not interested, off by default, lets each user hide a title from their own Web UI pages without hiding it for anyone else. A user with a parental rating limit sees the Web UI sections narrowed to the titles that limit allows, rather than none of them. The home Discover row, the Want to watch row, and the item page rows each have a placement setting; existing settings carry over. The Gaps Report's toolbar is grouped by what each control acts on, every header has a select-all, a line above the list says how many rows the filters hide, and Add to TODO is now Add to watchlist. The report is usable at phone width, and the settings page has collapsible sections, a search, and better screen reader support. A new scheduled task, Prune gaps from deleted items, takes deleted library items out of the report: a gap they were the only source of is removed, and one with other sources moves to the next. It has no default schedule; it waits for a running scan, and a second scan waits for the first. Recommendation groups link to the owned title they came from. Books get an OpenLibrary id field and albums and artists a Discogs id field in the metadata editor, with a link on the item's page; a dedicated OpenLibrary or Discogs plugin takes over when installed. Links are built from each title's ids when the report loads, so a link plugin installed later applies everywhere. The report takes far less memory and disk (on a library with 83,000 gaps, about 1.6 GB down to 200 MB in memory and 245 MB down to 131 MB on disk), loads in about half the time, and is written far less often during scans and where-to-watch lookups. Existing reports convert on first load; a report saved by this version cannot be read by an earlier one, so going back shows an empty report until its next scan.

10.11.10.0 - The Maintenance section has a Fulfillment queue for an administrator who fetches titles by hand. It folds every user's TODO list into one row per title, sorted by how many people still want it, names who is still waiting, and shows the streaming-service icons as soon as the queue opens, with the same links a TODO row already has. Mark fetched closes the title for every requester in one action, and Verify all checks the queue against the library and closes a title you already have, however it arrived. With Everyone's watchlist on (off by default), that same household list is a Discover source and leads the Discover view of every domain it has entries for. Send to the acquisition stack is done from the Gaps Report. The report's Send action has a quality profile picker, filled from the stack's own profile list and preselecting the profile you configured, so an older title the default profile cannot find a release for can still be sent. The report's My TODO list popup is gone; the Fulfillment queue is where an administrator sees every list. The report's multi-select bar can Acquire, Request, or Resolve a checked batch (Resolve applies one shared note), alongside Mint and Add to TODO. An administrator can manage another user's want-to-watch list. With "Want to watch: move arrived titles into a playlist" on, a title that is in the library moves into that user's own Jellyfin playlist the next time it is verified, so it shows up in every client. The playlist is named Want to Watch unless you change it, and only a real file counts as arrived. Amazon and web-search links for a book or album include the author or artist, on the report, the Web UI, and the Fulfillment queue. TMDB lists, Trakt lists, and OpenLibrary subjects are set with the same chip pickers the other curated sources use. A book's dialog loads its description from OpenLibrary when you open it. Studio pages, off by default, add a Missing from the studio row of that studio's movies you do not own, on the list page you open from a movie's studio credit. A library that sets a metadata fetcher order keeps TVmaze in the series check. TVmaze is not a Jellyfin metadata fetcher, so it is always asked and ranked last.

10.11.9.0 - Mind the Gaps now reaches into Jellyfin's own pages through an experimental, opt-in Web UI, with a master switch and one toggle per surface in settings, all off by default. A person's page lists what they made that you do not own, a movie or series page suggests titles like it that you are missing, an artist's page lists the albums you do not have, and a book page or an author's own page lists more by the same author. The home page can show a Discover row of the recommendations your scans found from titles you own and from lists that are public by nature (TMDB lists, Trakt lists, and TMDB's own feeds), never from a watchlist, wantlist, favorites, or a personal list. Click a card for a detail dialog with TMDB's synopsis, genres, runtime, rating, a trailer link, and a link to the title's JustWatch page, then send it to Radarr or Sonarr with the quality profile you pick; the dialog and the card grids can be driven from a keyboard or a TV remote. A user with a parental rating limit is shown none of these sections. With Want to watch turned on, every card carries a bookmark that adds the title to your own list, and the home page can show a Want to watch row of what you have listed and do not yet own. The TODO list is now kept per user, in the plugin's data folder, and removed when the user is deleted; the first administrator to open the old shared list takes it over, and an administrator can switch the report's TODO to everyone's lists to see and manage them. The Gaps Report loads faster: it fetches one tab at a time as slim rows, fetches a row's details only when you open it, revalidates what it already holds instead of downloading it again, and loads its script and stylesheet as separately cached files; the saved report is stored as one file per domain, and an existing report is converted automatically. A row shows up to two streaming-service icons, following your provider and monetization filters and wearing the service's logo (a service TMDB lists as several providers, such as a "with Ads" tier, shows as one icon and one provider filter entry), and clicking them opens the title's TMDB watch page. Gaps left behind by a source you have since removed or turned off are pruned on every scan, and a Prune stale gaps button under Maintenance does it right away. A TMDB list that cannot be read, such as a private one, no longer stops the other lists from being scanned, filling in a large library's series content is done in batches, and the scan log says how long each source took. New, and off by default: the report and the Web UI can load their posters, covers, and streaming-service logos through your server instead of each browser fetching them from TMDB and the other providers. Turn on "Keep the pages' images on this server" in the new Images section of settings; the server fetches each image once, from a fixed list of provider hosts only, keeps it under its cache folder, and sends the browser on to the provider whenever it cannot serve one, and a "Trim the image cache" scheduled task keeps the cache to the size you set (500 MB by default).

The report now links out everywhere: music rows link to MusicBrainz and Discogs, books to OpenLibrary, the Diagnose ids are clickable, and each creator or set group header links the source itself (an author's OpenLibrary page, an actor or director's TMDB page, an artist's MusicBrainz or Discogs page, a studio, keyword, label, or collection page); every link carries a per-provider CSS class, a data-provider attribute, and a title and aria-label, so a theme can inject service icons (the README has a ready-to-paste snippet under Advanced CSS customization). The library no longer reports a reboot's later seasons as missing episodes of the single-season original, a Name-plus- year match now prefers an exact-year hit over the one-year tolerance, and the Books (OpenLibrary) source is hardened against real-world author data. In settings, the Discogs toggle and token sit in the Data sources section, and Markdown exports are named by domain so different tabs no longer overwrite each other.

Breaking change: the old free-text studio-names field was removed in favor of the chip picker, so any studios configured by name (rather than id) are dropped and must be re-picked.

10.11.1.0 - Initial release. Mind the Gaps scans your library and builds a dashboard todo list of what is missing or worth adding: movies missing from a collection or franchise; missing seasons and episodes (optionally cross-checked against TVmaze and TheTVDB); films from an owned actor or director's filmography (with an independent Trakt cross-check); curated studio and keyword sets; and TMDB recommendations.
